## P17 — Design research: universality and release proof



## 0. Invariants

- P17 is acceptance, not a feature phase. A failed product assertion returns to its owning
  P1–P16 item; P17 may add fixtures, gates, release tooling and evidence, but does not repair the
  product behind a red assertion.
- All package and consumer tests install exported archives into a fresh temporary directory with a
  fresh `COMPOSER_HOME`. The repository root, root `vendor/`, Composer path repositories and
  `packages/*` are absent from the runtime autoloader.
- The candidate version is `1.0.0`. Composer package versions come from immutable VCS tags; no
  `version` field is added to package `composer.json`.
- The release cohort is derived from executed P1/P15 metadata, then frozen in a digest-qualified
  candidate manifest. It is not copied from the current directory names because D89/D90 may change
  package identities before P17.
- `flex/crm` is a consumer, not part of the CoreX release cohort. The `import-export` tombstone has
  no package. Private/public distribution channel is retained per package; P17 never changes
  repository visibility.
- One root `CHANGELOG.md` is the release ledger. Per-package changelogs are package documentation,
  not a second release ledger, and P17 does not manufacture parallel `[Unreleased]` histories.
- G-RELEASE authorizes only the exact immutable publication packet. Preflight, fixture execution,
  artifact construction and remote read-only reconciliation run before the gate.
- A skipped, stale, path-repository-backed or monorepo-autoload-backed check is red.

## 1. Definition of Done 1.0: exactly 27 executable assertions

The non-normative audit says “27” but contains 25 bullets (`audits/2026-09-19-perplexity-3.md`
lines 2842–2872). D95 preserves all 25 meanings, adapts the product-specific CMS wording to the
repository doctrine, and adds the two acceptance promises already made by the plan. The machine
IDs below are stable and are the only order used by `dod-1.0.json`.

| ID | Assertion | Owning evidence |
|:--|:--|:--|
| DOD-01 | Every live package has a one-sentence purpose. | P1 taxonomy + README gate |
| DOD-02 | Package taxonomy is machine-checked. | P3 package graph/taxonomy gate |
| DOD-03 | `corex/core` is foundation-only, not a capability warehouse. | P6 zone inventory and ratchet |
| DOD-04 | Every public symbol is present in the declared API map. | P1 metadata + P3 R4/BC gate |
| DOD-05 | Cross-package imports of implementation internals are forbidden. | P3 R2 planted-negative receipt |
| DOD-06 | Every owned table has one declared owner. | P2 catalogue + P3 table-owner gate |
| DOD-07 | Configuration is validated and injected as typed options. | P7 config gate |
| DOD-08 | Contextual state is safe across Octane/request/queue boundaries. | P4/P8/P11 worker receipts |
| DOD-09 | Durable messages are scalar-serializable and versioned. | P5/P11 durable-message gates |
| DOD-10 | Attributes do not depend on model/table identity. | P10 attribute identity tests |
| DOD-11 | Attribute definition source is replaceable through a public contract. | P10 source contract suite |
| DOD-12 | Transfer proves resume, idempotency and partial-failure behavior. | Transfer package contract tests |
| DOD-13 | Search has at least two independently tested provider implementations. | base + Meilisearch provider receipts |
| DOD-14 | Meilisearch is optional. | P17 profile without Meilisearch |
| DOD-15 | Search Intl is removable. | P17 profile without Search Intl |
| DOD-16 | Bridge packages own no foreign data. | P2 ownership + P3 graph gate |
| DOD-17 | Large packages match their bounded-context-first structural profile. | P9/P16 final receipts |
| DOD-18 | Service providers remain composition roots. | P8 provider-size/composition gate |
| DOD-19 | FlexCRM and an independent non-CRM/CMS/Store consumer use the same public lower-level contracts. | FlexCRM suites + P17 equipment-registry consumer |
| DOD-20 | Custom external extensions pass the reusable contract suite. | P17 five-fixture matrix |
| DOD-21 | Upgrade from every applicable previous supported package version is reproduced. | P17 upgrade proof |
| DOD-22 | PHP/API/schema compatibility diff is part of the release gate. | P3/P13/P14 gates + P17 candidate |
| DOD-23 | Accepted architecture decisions and current code do not diverge. | decision-to-check map + plan lint |
| DOD-24 | Examples use only supported public API. | fixture import/public-surface gate |
| DOD-25 | Every package README covers minimal install, configuration, extension and failure semantics. | README contract gate |
| DOD-26 | Every supported install profile boots from split archives in a pristine consumer. | P17 profile matrix |
| DOD-27 | A useful application with no Flex/CRM/CMS/Store dependency passes its behavioral smoke suite. | P17 equipment-registry consumer |

`DOD-19` does not claim a CoreX-owned CMS. The independent fixture is deliberately outside CRM,
CMS and Store vocabulary and proves the stronger doctrine in `docs/dev-doctrine.md` §1.

## 2. Release cohort and candidate manifest (P17.1)

The candidate builder reads every executed `packages/*/composer.json`, validates the P1 metadata,
and emits `artifacts/P17/release-cohort.json` with this shape:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "corex-release-cohort/1",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "source_commit": "<40-hex>",
  "packages": [
    {
      "name": "corex/example",
      "path": "packages/example",
      "distribution": "public|private",
      "mirror": "owner/repository",
      "tree_sha256": "<64-hex>",
      "archive_sha256": "<64-hex>",
      "composer_sha256": "<64-hex>"
    }
  ],
  "excluded": [
    {"path": "packages/crm", "reason": "flex-product-consumer"},
    {"path": "packages/import-export", "reason": "tombstone"}
  ]
}
```

Rules:

1. Names and paths are read after D89/D90; no P17 constant assumes `corex/api` or `corex/auth`.
2. Every live `corex/*` package is present exactly once. A new/missing package is a hard error.
3. Export uses the existing allowlist policy: production package files only, never tests, root
   autoload, secrets, plans or sibling package paths.
4. Two independent exports from the same commit produce byte-identical archives and metadata.
5. A local Composer repository is built only from those archives. All later fixtures install from
   that repository with `preferred-install=dist` and no path/VCS repository.
6. The public/private channel and mirror mapping come from the existing distribution policy and
   are frozen in the manifest. Unknown channel or mirror is red.

The CLI is exact:

```text
python3 scripts/distribution/release_candidate.py build --version 1.0.0 --output <temp>
python3 scripts/distribution/release_candidate.py verify --candidate <temp>/candidate.json
```

`verify` rejects dirty-source export, wrong commit, missing package, unexpected file, absolute
workspace path, non-deterministic archive and dependency on a cohort member absent from metadata.

## 3. External extension fixtures (P17.2)

Five standalone Composer packages live under `fixtures/extensions/`:

| Fixture | Public contract exercised | Observable proof |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `custom-search-provider` | search provider/driver contract | index + query through the public manager |
| `custom-attribute-source` | attribute definition source | compile definitions from fixture-owned scalar data |
| `custom-transfer-codec` | transfer source/sink/codec boundary | checkpointed round-trip with one typed row failure |
| `custom-panel-provider` | panel declaration/catalogue projection | deterministic descriptor contribution and freeze |
| `custom-workflow-activity` | workflow activity/definition contribution | exact id/version stamp and mismatch rejection |

Each fixture has its own `composer.json`, PSR-4 namespace `ThirdParty\\...`, package tests and
module/registration entry point. It may import only namespaces declared by the installed package's
`extra.corex.public-api`; the public-surface gate checks the installed archive metadata, not the
monorepo source. Each fixture runs P11 `ExtensionContract::verify()` where applicable and a
point-specific behavior assertion. A planted import of one `Internal` symbol must fail with the
package and symbol in the diagnostic.

## 4. External API clients (P17.3–P17.4)

Clients are protocol fixtures, not Laravel packages and not generated SDKs:

- REST reads discovery/OpenAPI, executes one query and one command, follows only response-provided
  cursor tokens, retries an idempotent mutation with the same key and checks both error media types.
- MCP reads the published tool schema, invokes the same operation through the shared invoker and
  proves result/error parity with REST.
- Bulk submits, polls, cancels one bounded operation, downloads the declared result and observes a
  per-row failure without assuming rollback of completed rows.
- Webhook registers only a declared topic, verifies exact signed bytes with fixture-owned synthetic
  keys, deduplicates on delivery identity, fails a tampered signature and exercises bounded replay
  against a local receiver only.

All clients validate the committed `api/v1/{openapi,operations,errors,webhooks,manifest}.json`
before behavior. They may not include a CoreX class, container bootstrap or internal DTO. GraphQL is
absent. Network egress is restricted to the local test server/receiver.

## 5. Independent non-product consumer (P17.5)

`fixtures/consumers/equipment-registry` is a minimal Laravel application for tracking equipment,
inspection attributes and maintenance workflow. It is not a CMS, CRM or Store and contains no
`flex/*`, `Flex\\`, commerce, customer, lead, deal, content-page or storefront dependency/vocabulary.

It installs CoreX archives from the candidate repository and uses public contracts for:

- entity/module declaration and freeze;
- replaceable attributes for inspection fields;
- base search provider (no Meilisearch);
- transfer import with checkpoint/partial-failure report;
- workflow activity and a worker wakeup;
- optional REST exposure through the published operation contract.

The smoke suite creates an equipment record, resolves an attribute definition, indexes and finds
it, imports a second row with one controlled failure, schedules one maintenance activity, restarts
the worker boundary and reads the result. A scan rejects all Flex and internal namespace imports.

## 6. Pristine installation and compatibility matrix (P17.6)

The profile manifest contains exactly these behavior profiles:

| Profile | Required properties |
|:--|:--|
| `bare-single` | `corex/core`; single database; no modules, tenancy, Meilisearch, Search Intl or HTTP |
| `modular-single` | modules plus representative attributes/search/transfer/workflow packages; SQLite |
| `modular-multi` | modules + tenancy + SQL-owning capabilities; two physical tenant databases; PostgreSQL |
| `worker-only` | CLI/queue bootstrap with no HTTP route requirement; wakeup/workflow/tasks path |
| `search-portable` | base search + Intl bridge, no Meilisearch package/class/config requirement |
| `full-corex` | every package in the frozen cohort on its declared distribution channel |

Every run creates a Laravel consumer in a new temp directory and a new Composer cache/home, installs
only candidate dist archives, runs `composer validate`, optimized strict PSR-4 autoload, Laravel
package discovery, config boot and the profile probe. Generated Composer metadata must contain no
workspace path. Uninstall profiles remove the optional package, rebuild autoload and boot again.

Compatibility is derived from each package's declared PHP/Illuminate constraints. For every cohort
package the matrix covers the lowest and highest supported PHP/Laravel major pair and one
`--prefer-lowest --prefer-stable` resolution. Unsupported combinations are excluded by a recorded
constraint calculation, never by a skipped failing job. Behavioral profiles run on Laravel 12 and
13 where the union of their packages declares both; a narrower package such as auth remains on its
declared range and does not make an unsupported lane green.

## 7. Upgrade proof (P17.7)

`release-baselines.json` is generated from read-only remote/package metadata, then reviewed and
pinned. Each row has package, prior version, distribution channel, immutable ref, archive digest and
reason. The baseline is the most recent supported immutable package release, not a monorepo tag.

For an applicable package the proof:

1. installs the baseline dist into a pristine consumer;
2. creates the package's public persisted/runtime fixture using baseline code;
3. records public API/schema/config snapshots and fixture checksums;
4. changes only the repository metadata and constraint to the exact `1.0.0` candidate;
5. runs Composer update, package discovery and declared migrations/upgrade commands;
6. verifies preserved data, idempotent rerun, public API compatibility and current behavior.

A genuinely never-published package may use `not-applicable/new-package`, but only with remote
absence evidence in the baseline manifest; it still runs clean install. Failure after a migration
must be forward-recoverable in a disposable database. No tag, mirror or registry write occurs.

## 8. Final scorecard and documentation contract (P17.8)

P17 reruns the P2 scorecard generator with the same 12 criteria and no average/total. The final
document shows every `<2` cell with its exact failing measurement. A low score is not by itself a
release veto; a red DOD assertion is.

The README/example gate checks each cohort package for four headings or declared equivalents:
minimal installation, configuration/defaults, extension/public seams and failure semantics. Code
blocks compile in a pristine installed consumer and imports are checked against the installed
public API map. Missing content is returned to the owning producer phase; P17 does not invent
package behavior in documentation.

## 9. Executable DoD manifest and gate (P17.9–P17.10)

`scripts/dod-1.0.json` is the normative machine manifest. Each of its exactly 27 records contains:

```json
{
  "id": "DOD-01",
  "statement": "...",
  "owner": ["P1.2", "P17.10"],
  "mode": "live-command|candidate-receipt",
  "command": ["..."],
  "receipt": "plans/.../findings/...json",
  "freshness_inputs": ["path-or-glob"],
  "negative_fixture": "fixture-id"
}
```

Exactly one of `command` or `receipt` is active per assertion. Receipt assertions bind source
commit, environment, manifest digest, command argv/exit code and input digests; stale or skipped is
red. The generator renders `docs/architecture/dod-1.0.md` from JSON and `--check` rejects drift.

```text
python3 scripts/dod-1.0.py check --candidate <candidate.json>
python3 scripts/dod-1.0.py explain DOD-20
python3 scripts/dod-1.0.py render --check
```

The checker produces one JSON result with 27 rows and summary counts. It never converts `unknown`,
`skipped`, `stale` or `not-run` to pass. P17.10 plants at least these failures and removes them in
`try/finally`: missing API-map symbol, foreign Internal import, stale receipt commit, monorepo path in
autoload metadata, omitted profile and a 26-row manifest.

## 10. Release candidate, G-RELEASE and forward-only publication (P17.11–P17.12)

P17.11 is read/write-local and routine. It changes `extra.corex.stability` from `experimental` to
`stable` for the frozen CoreX cohort only, regenerates the candidate, then runs:

- all affected package lint/analyse/test and isolated PostgreSQL lanes;
- root lint/analyse/test/PG, architecture, package graph, naming, public-surface and BC gates;
- API snapshot generation `--check` and compatibility against the prior supported release;
- anti-weakening and full mutation checks;
- extension/client/consumer/profile/upgrade matrices;
- the 27-row DoD gate;
- a second byte-identical candidate build and remote read-only collision/pre-existence checks.

It emits `publication-packet/v1` with exact source commit, version, cohort/candidate/DoD digests and
one ordered operation per destination. Any remote mismatch, missing permission, dirty source,
red/skipped/stale check or non-deterministic rebuild is NO-GO. No external write occurs.

P17.12 is `manual` and has Authority G-RELEASE. The owner grant must bind the exact publication
packet digest. The publisher reconciles each remote immediately before its operation, allows only
absent or byte-identical no-op state, and records every result append-only. It never creates an
undeclared repository, changes visibility, force-pushes, deletes/rewrites a tag, provisions a secret
or publishes an unlisted registry package. Order is split commit/ref → split tag → release →
root tag → post-publication install by exact tag. A partial failure resumes from the same packet;
an already published bad immutable artifact requires a new forward release, never history rewrite.

P17 closes only when post-publication consumers resolve the exact released refs/digests and the
publication ledger has no unknown/collision/unperformed operation. Release authorization is not
inferred from a green preflight.

## 11. Item dependency map

`P17.1` freezes the candidate source. `P17.2`–`P17.5` are independent after it. `P17.6` waits
for P17.2/P17.5 so profiles include the externality proofs; P17.7 depends only on P17.1 and pinned
remote baselines. P17.8 is independent after all producer phases. `P17.9` waits for P17.2–P17.8;
`P17.10` waits for P17.9. `P17.11` waits for every routine item. `P17.12` is last and remains
blocked on the exact G-RELEASE grant.
